topics.title: Flutter and Dart
topics.technical: Flutter builds native apps for mobile, web and desktop from one Dart codebase, rendering its own widgets for consistent pixels everywhere. Dart is a typed, familiar language compiled ahead-of-time for release speed.
topics.simple: One codebase, real apps on every device — written in an approachable typed language.

topics.title: Dart fundamentals
topics.technical: Variables, types, functions, null safety, classes and async/await form Dart's core; sound null safety moves a whole bug class to compile time. Comfort here makes the framework above it click.
topics.simple: The language basics — with a type system that refuses most crashes before they happen.

topics.title: Everything is a widget
topics.technical: Flutter's UI is a tree of widgets — structural, layout and styling — that you compose and nest. Stateless widgets are pure functions of their inputs; stateful ones hold changing data. Composition replaces inheritance.
topics.simple: You build screens by nesting small building blocks called widgets.

topics.title: Layout widgets
topics.technical: Row, Column, Stack, Container, Padding and Expanded arrange the tree; constraints flow down and sizes flow up. Understanding Flutter's constraint model is the difference between fluent layout and fighting overflow errors.
topics.simple: Arranging widgets in rows, columns and stacks — once you grasp how sizing flows.

topics.title: Styling and theming
topics.technical: Themes centralise colours, typography and shapes so a whole app restyles from one place; Material and Cupertino give platform-idiomatic components. Consistent theming is what separates polished apps from prototypes.
topics.simple: Setting your app's look once so every screen matches.

topics.title: Handling user input
topics.technical: Buttons, text fields, gestures and forms capture interaction; controllers read field values and form validation guards submission. Responsive, validated input is the backbone of any real app.
topics.simple: Buttons, taps and text fields — how the app listens to the user.

topics.title: State management basics
topics.technical: setState rebuilds a stateful widget when its data changes — the starting point every Flutter dev learns before reaching for bigger tools. Knowing when a rebuild happens is core to correctness and speed.
topics.simple: Telling Flutter 'this changed, redraw it' — the foundation of interactivity.

topics.title: Navigation and routing
topics.technical: Navigator pushes and pops screens as a stack; named routes and arguments pass data between them. Deep links and back-button behaviour turn a demo into an app people can actually use.
topics.simple: Moving between screens and carrying data along.

topics.title: Lists and scrolling
topics.technical: ListView and GridView render long, scrollable collections lazily, building only visible items; builders keep large lists smooth. Most app screens are lists, so this pattern recurs everywhere.
topics.simple: Showing long scrollable lists without loading everything at once.

topics.title: Async and futures
topics.technical: Network and disk work returns Futures consumed with async/await; FutureBuilder and StreamBuilder render loading, error and data states declaratively. Modelling those three states honestly is what makes apps feel solid.
topics.simple: Fetching data in the background and showing loading, error or result cleanly.

topics.title: Calling REST APIs
topics.technical: The http package sends requests and decodes JSON into Dart objects; real code checks status, handles failure, and separates networking from UI. The API contract is the seam between app and server.
topics.simple: Your app phones a server for data and turns the JSON reply into something it can show.

topics.title: Advanced state management
topics.technical: As apps grow, Provider or Riverpod share state across the tree without prop-drilling, separating business logic from widgets. Choosing and applying one consistently keeps large apps maintainable.
topics.simple: Sharing data across many screens cleanly once setState is not enough.

topics.title: Local storage
topics.technical: shared_preferences stores small key-value data; sqflite or Hive persist structured data offline. Deciding what to cache and when to sync is what makes apps usable without signal.
topics.simple: Saving data on the device so the app works offline and remembers settings.

topics.title: Firebase integration
topics.technical: Firebase supplies auth, Firestore, storage and messaging with little backend code; real-time listeners update the UI as data changes server-side. It is the fastest path from idea to backed app.
topics.simple: A ready-made backend — logins, database, notifications — with almost no server code.

topics.title: Animations
topics.technical: Implicit animations tween properties automatically; explicit ones use controllers for fine control; Hero animations bridge screens. Motion, used with restraint, is what makes an app feel alive rather than clever.
topics.simple: Smooth movement and transitions that make the app feel polished.

topics.title: Responsive and adaptive UI
topics.technical: LayoutBuilder and MediaQuery adapt to screen size and orientation; adaptive widgets match platform conventions. One codebase must look right from a small phone to a tablet.
topics.simple: Making one app look right on every screen size and shape.

topics.title: Platform features
topics.technical: Plugins reach the camera, location, notifications and sensors; permissions must be requested and handled gracefully. Native capability is where apps become more than styled websites.
topics.simple: Using the phone's real powers — camera, GPS, notifications — through plugins.

topics.title: Testing Flutter apps
topics.technical: Unit tests check logic, widget tests render and interact with UI, integration tests drive whole flows. Tests let you refactor a growing app without breaking screens silently.
topics.simple: Robots that press your app's buttons to prove screens still work.

topics.title: Performance and debugging
topics.technical: Flutter DevTools profiles rebuilds, frames and memory; const widgets and keys cut needless work. Smooth 60fps is engineered by measurement, not hoped for.
topics.simple: Finding and fixing the jank so the app stays buttery smooth.

topics.title: Building and releasing
topics.technical: Release builds, signing, app icons and store submission ship the app; flavors separate dev from production. An app in a store, updatable, is the definition of done.
topics.simple: Turning your project into an installable app on the real app stores.

topics.title: The capstone
topics.technical: Ship a complete app: multiple screens, state management, a REST or Firebase backend, local persistence, animations, tests, and a release build. It is the portfolio artifact that demonstrates the whole journey.
topics.simple: One finished, installable app that uses everything above.
